summary: 1939 Civilian Conservation Corps lookout tower in The Channels Natural Area Preserve, Washington County, Virginia; in use until 1970; NHLR-registered 2014.

access.note: Reached on foot about three miles from VA Route 80 at Hayters Gap, on a private dirt road open to hikers only by easement. The register does not say whether the tower may be climbed.

visit.trail_note: About three miles on foot from a parking lot on VA Route 80 at Hayters Gap, then forest roads.

events.note: Built by Civilian Conservation Corps men; materials carried to the site on mules and the men's backs
Register says the tower was in use until the spring of 1970; it does not say staffed
Registered December 15, 2014 as US 1051, VA 20; nominated by Reginald B. Childers

notes_for_editor: Record matches the register: built 1939, in use until spring 1970, VDOF-administered, in Washington County, registered 2014 (nominated by Reginald B. Childers). The register gives no status after 1970; the only later item is a photo captioned September 2020, so the story says post-1970 condition is unclear and does not claim the tower stands. Not climbable: no source gives it, so no visit.climbable key and the story does not encourage climbing. The SMLiv hiking article walks past 'the abandoned fire tower' on the way to The Channels and separately describes 'the Middle Knob fire tower'; it names neither, so identifying the abandoned tower with this lookout is not established. Article date unknown. Unverified leads, not used: a search snippet attributed to Visit Abingdon says the fire tower remains are not open to the public, but that page redirected (HTTP 307) and was not read; a snippet dated the status to March 20, 2010, but no source was read for it. Staffing names, design and height are not in any source read. No new photos. No corrections proposed.
